y1: John the Baptist was killed at Herod Antipas' birthday banquet. It was a banquet where the ruler's prestige and oath were more important than the life of a righteous man.
y2: Hearing the news, Jesus went to a deserted place to be alone. He needed time to grieve. But when the crowd followed Him, Jesus was not annoyed; He had compassion on them. Even in His sorrow, His love did not stop.
y3: The banquet in the palace brought death, while the banquet in the wilderness brought life. Matthew puts the two stories side by side to show who the “true King” is.
y4: You give them something to eat
y5: The disciples offered a realistic solution: “Send the crowds away.” Jesus says, “They don't need to go away. You give them something to eat.” He entrusted the impossible to the disciples.
y6: “He took them, looked up to heaven, gave thanks, broke the loaves, and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowds.” These verbs (take, give thanks, break, give) are repeated exactly at the Last Supper (26:26).
y7: Feeding the people in the wilderness recalls the manna in the book of Exodus. The twelve baskets may symbolize the twelve tribes. Jesus is more than a new Moses; He is God who feeds His people.
y9: Jesus sent the crowds away, went up on the mountain by Himself, and prayed. Meanwhile, the disciples were fighting a headwind all night. “The fourth watch of the night” is between 3 and 6 a.m. Jesus came at the most exhausting and darkest time.
y10: “Cheer up! It is I, do not be afraid!” In Greek, it is “ego eimi”, meaning “I am”. This sounds the same as the name by which God revealed Himself to Moses as “I AM WHO I AM” (Exodus 3:14).
y11: Job 9:8 calls God the one who “tramples the waves of the sea”. In the Old Testament, the sea is a symbol of chaos. Jesus is the Creator walking on that chaos.
y13: Peter boldly stepped out onto the water. The other disciples stayed in the boat. But “he saw the wind and was afraid” and began to sink. The situation was the same, but his focus changed.
y14: Jesus “immediately” reached out His hand and caught him. “You of little faith, why did you doubt?” The hand came before the rebuke. For the first time, those in the boat worshiped Him, saying, “You are truly the Son of God.”
y15: Peter sank, but he was the only disciple who walked on the water. Only the one who steps out of the boat experiences failure. Jesus catches him even as he sinks. Doubt (distazo) means “being double-minded”.
verse: “Immediately Jesus reached out his hand and caught him. ‘You of little faith,’ he said, ‘why did you doubt?’ … Then those who were in the boat worshiped him, saying, ‘Truly you are the Son of God.’”
prayer: Jesus, I praise You for having compassion on the crowd even in Your sorrow and for feeding so many with so little. Let me hear Your voice coming over the storm, saying, “Cheer up, it is I.” Let me look at You instead of the wind, and trust in Your hand that catches me when I sink. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
d0: have compassion. It appears again after 9:36. Jesus' miracles were not a display of power, but came from this heart. The same word is found in 15:32 and 20:34.
d1: give thanks. The Jews prayed, “Blessed are You, our God, who brings forth bread from the earth.” The same verb is used at the Last Supper (26:26).
d2: It is I. Although it is a simple “It is I”, it echoes the “I AM WHO I AM” of Exodus 3:14. There are seven “ego eimi” statements in the Gospel of John, such as “I am the bread of life”.
d3: worship. This is the action the wise men did to the baby Jesus in chapter 2. The disciples worship Jesus as the Son of God for the first time. Compare with “Worship the Lord your God” in 4:10.
